checks: Source db95f50a50308952 §3 (4)–(5) concerns whole-majorant reciprocal measures. The frozen statement assumes the pointed fiber and denominator form rather than using the earlier selected-minimum homothety argument.

The physical map T is a homothety of positive factor a from the reference fiber onto the entire other fiber. Its Jacobian is a^d and the denominator is multiplied by a, with the same M_j. The quotient gives a^(d−1), including exact mass preservation in d=1. Constant-denominator cube calculations at a=3/2 verified the exponents in dimensions 1–3.

The untruncated logarithmic rate shifts by −λ_j log a. Positive-part truncation is 1-Lipschitz, so the discrepancy between the two truncated rates is uniformly bounded by λ_j|log a|→0, including around zero.

Finite weak convergence gives tightness and bounded masses. The affine physical maps converge uniformly on compact sets, and the rate discrepancy is uniform. Bounded continuous tests therefore give the whole limiting measure identity, which can be restricted to any Borel rate tail even if its endpoint is an atom.
